MX-D-READ.section: Registering an MCP server; Configuring MCP tools; Managing connections
MX-D-READ.assertion: Registration, association and tool selection are separate; removal and credential replacement have dependent-connection consequences.
A custom agent accesses only its assigned tools.

MX-D-TOPOLOGY.section: How topology graphs are created; Resource discovery; Investigation scope beyond topology
MX-D-TOPOLOGY.assertion: Discovery and relationship inference produce a representation that does not bound investigation permissions.

MX-D-TOPOLOGY.section: How memory is built and refreshed
MX-D-TOPOLOGY.assertion: Managed stores have distinct refresh conditions and can be inspected after regeneration.

MX-D-RECALL.section: How memories work; Activating and deactivating; Deleting a memory store
MX-D-RECALL.assertion: Description-led retrieval, immutable versions and activation differ from irreversible custom-store deletion.

MX-D-FEEDBACK.assertion: Feedback records the actual cause; latest feedback and separate sharing confirmation have distinct effects.
Corrective lessons are retained for future relevant investigations.

MX-D-INSTRUCTIONS.section: How agent instructions work; Agent type scoping
MX-D-INSTRUCTIONS.assertion: Instructions are loaded at session start; existing sessions retain the original content.

MX-D-SKILL.assertion: Description, target scope and supported content determine applicability.
Custom definitions load assigned skill documents.

MX-D-TRIAGE.assertion: Linked, Skipped and Proceed are routing outcomes; supported corrections reschedule independent work.

MX-D-INVESTIGATE.assertion: Manual scope and operator context drive a separate investigation record.

MX-D-INVESTIGATE.section: Custom agents compared to built-in capabilities
MX-D-INVESTIGATE.assertion: Incident response is a built-in path, not a mandatory custom-agent task.

MX-D-CUSTOM.assertion: Prompt, selected tools and assigned skills are loaded per invocation.

MX-D-CUSTOM.section: Running; Canceling an invocation; Tool call results
MX-D-CUSTOM.assertion: Runs have history; cancellation preserves completed evidence and may not interrupt in-flight calls.

MX-D-CUSTOM.section: Creating a custom agent using the form
MX-D-CUSTOM.assertion: Creation and tool assignment are separate setup concerns.

MX-D-SCHEDULE.assertion: Rate/cron triggers can be paused or deleted separately from invocations.
The schedule anchors a flexible window of up to 30 minutes.

MX-D-PREVENT.assertion: Evaluation control and recommendation disposition are separate; unretained recommendations may age out.

MX-D-ACTION.section: Enabling; Registering elevated role; Categorizing tools; Approving directed actions
MX-D-ACTION.assertion: Independent opt-ins, operation-specific approval, preference replacement and classification govern mutation.

MX-D-READINESS.section: Getting started; Performing a code review; Automatic verification testing
MX-D-READINESS.assertion: Review and verification settings are independent; candidate and verification results are inspectable.
Release-management eligibility differs from production operations.

MX-D-TEST.section: How release testing works; Defining test profiles; Reviewing results
MX-D-TEST.assertion: Testing sends real requests including writes and reports observed results.
Release testing is a feature-specific preview path.

MX-S-CONTEXT.section: Register once, reuse everywhere; One connection, shared across capabilities
MX-S-CONTEXT.assertion: Registration, resource association and write opt-ins are distinct.

MX-S-ACCESS.section: Configure penetration test scope; Configure VPC resources
MX-S-ACCESS.assertion: Targets, supporting accessible URLs and excluded paths have different purposes.
Failed preflight stops testing and must be inspected separately.

MX-S-AUTH.section: Use advanced setting; Configure multiple credentials
MX-S-AUTH.assertion: Resource retrieval and application login are separate; strategy-specific permissions and limits apply.

MX-S-LOGIN.assertion: Successful navigation produces a skill reused in later sessions/runs; disabling reuse preserves learning.

MX-S-RUN.section: Penetration testing: reusable configurations with independent executions
MX-S-RUN.assertion: One configuration supports separate runs and new findings.
Saving, executing and preflight outcomes are different stages.

MX-S-FINDING.section: Default confidence filter; Review finding details; View original agent version
MX-S-FINDING.assertion: Evidence, display filtering and original/latest attributes are distinct review surfaces.

MX-S-FIX.assertion: Current guidance distinguishes private-repository proposals and S3 diffs.
Repository writes are separately configured and provider-limited.

MX-S-REVALIDATE.section: Select findings; Interpret results; Trace history
MX-S-REVALIDATE.assertion: Replay has separate job identity, selected scope and preserved original finding.

MX-S-CRITERIA.section: Overview; Enable or disable a pack
MX-S-CRITERIA.assertion: Enabled packs govern future eligible reviews and have distinct applicability/compliance fields.
Design reviews distinguish Insufficient data and Not applicable from compliance/violation.

MX-S-GENERATE.section: Generate requirements; Replace requirements with a new upload
MX-S-GENERATE.assertion: Generation replaces existing pack contents and requires review before use.

MX-S-CODE.section: Create and run a code review; Review findings
MX-S-CODE.assertion: Source preflight precedes analysis and has inspectable failure outcomes.

MX-S-CODE.section: How code review works; Filtering findings
MX-S-CODE.assertion: Change-trigger and main-branch filtering behavior are distinct configuration paths.

MX-S-DESIGN.assertion: Design reviews have a different one-off lifecycle.
Missing evidence and non-compliance differ; cloning creates a new review.

MX-S-THREAT.section: Create and run a threat model; Review threats
MX-S-THREAT.assertion: Scope documents and source context have distinct roles; overview and threats are reviewable.

MX-S-PIPELINE.assertion: The integration invokes an existing configured test, uses OIDC and observes server-side work.

MX-S-JIRA.section: Connecting projects to an Agent Space
MX-S-JIRA.assertion: Create and comment actions are selected per project.
The selected project must allow Task and receives one issue per selected finding.
Previously created issues are not deleted with the integration.

MX-F-QUERY.assertion: Cost Explorer, anomaly detection, optimization services and CloudTrail supply distinct evidence.
Recommendations are upstream analysis; anomaly causality remains investigative.

MX-F-FILES.section: Supported file types; Manage context files
MX-F-FILES.assertion: Files are agent-read-only, size-limited and support soft deletion/restoration.
File removal and other object lifecycles differ.

MX-F-MEMORY.assertion: Remember, update and forget govern retained preferences/corrections.
Instance isolation and memory updates differ from conversation retention.

MX-F-COMPACT.assertion: Automatic summarization replaces older context while recent messages remain in full.

MX-F-TASK.assertion: Tasks are explicit and run through a shared queue rather than blocking the conversation.
Cancellation and record removal are different lifecycle operations.

MX-F-SCHEDULE.assertion: Schedules create automations and new tasks; disabling/deleting stops recurring work.
Automations and task records have distinct lifecycles.

MX-F-EVENT.section: Prerequisites; Verify and manage the automation
MX-F-EVENT.assertion: Monitor, managed-rule permissions and saved condition create a traceable automation/task path.
The supported preview trigger is a cost-anomaly event.

MX-F-ARTIFACT.assertion: Reports are artifacts, default to HTML and can be revised through follow-up.
Artifacts and other retained objects have distinct controls.

MX-F-JIRA.section: Jira issue creation and comment addition
MX-F-JIRA.assertion: Approval differs between interactive/on-demand and automated invocation.
Project connections and supported actions limit the effect.

MX-F-SLACK.assertion: Connections are per-instance/channel and one-way; membership is required.
Posting does not prompt for approval even in interactive invocation.

MX-D-QUERY.section: Custom agents compared to built-in capabilities
MX-D-QUERY.assertion: On-demand queries are a built-in path; custom agents are separately configured.

MX-D-QUERY.section: Configuring MCP tools in an Agent Space
MX-D-QUERY.assertion: Connected evidence remains subject to selected source tools.

MX-S-PERSONALIZE.section: How personalization learns from your edits; Enable or disable Findings Personalization
MX-S-PERSONALIZE.assertion: Learning uses eligible edits from the most recent completed run; false-positive status is special, and disabling preserves preferences.

qualifications: Some official direct-page and indexed-page revisions differ; relevant record notes identify those differences.
State labels are logical explanations, not invented API enum names.
Similarity algorithms, ranking, exact retry guarantees and unsupported recovery operations remain undocumented.
